content.comment_body: I'm using a [product_name] with [version_no] to monitor my HVAC system and control the humidifier. After 35 and 50 days of uptime, it has locked up twice. When this occurs, it doesn't respond to inputs and the HMI screen and soft keys freeze. Interestingly, the web server interface still responds, but displays outdated information since the hardware isn't processing input changes. Software tools like [product_name] allow connection and online testing, but cannot resolve the issue; only a manual power cycle helps. It's frustrating since the web server appears normal, but the physical keys reveal the device has stopped responding. Has anyone else come across this? Is there a solution or is my unit defective?

Based on what you described, this seems to be a firmware issue with the [product_name] [version_no]. Several users in both English and German forums have reported similar errors. You should initiate a support request or submit a warranty claim. Newer hardware revisions, such as [version_no] with updated firmware and new operator devices, have been mentioned in user reports.
We're also experiencing the same lock-up problem on several [product_name] units. So far, we haven't found a solution.
See the reply above your post. Consider reaching out for Support.
Check out this discussion: Product information regarding [product_name] [version_no] hardware issues.

Thank you for clarifying. [company_name] has documented the problem as: "The display (integrated display, operator device, and web server) fails to refresh." Interestingly, the web server continues to function even when the onboard display and keys do not respond. The main concern is that inputs aren't refreshed, which isn't mentioned in their note. I performed a firmware update today and will report back after some time.
Did the firmware update go as planned? How can you confirm it worked? Is there a new firmware version visible?

The update was successful and only took a minute. Afterward, you can verify the firmware version through Diagnostics > Software > FW Version, which will show the latest version (e.g., 1.81.03 for newer hardware, while older hardware shows 1.81.01). Upgrading [product_name] software to the appropriate version is also necessary.
A further observation: the web server is actually displaying [version_no].
Is it truly possible to upgrade the firmware of the [product_name] [version_no] hardware to the newer version? How is the firmware update performed?
Hello [user_name], review the full discussion and you'll find your answer—especially in my post from 10/7/2017 11:42 AM.
All done. Thank you. I've understood now that updating the firmware for [product_name] is indeed possible. I was confused earlier due to another recent discussion stating otherwise.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report persistent lock-up issues affecting [product_name] modules over prolonged operation, notably in HVAC monitoring and control scenarios. When lock-ups occur, the modules stop responding to inputs, and displays freeze, yet the web server interface continues to work and shows outdated data. Diagnostics tools can connect but cannot fix the issue except by power-cycling the unit. Community consensus attributes this to a firmware defect specific to certain hardware versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] hardware and its interfaces to function reliably over extended periods, accurately handle inputs, and present correct system status via both local and remote displays.
